units: reference units (dependent 8-byte iadd step = 2); the simulator converts to real cycles (x1.049)
memory_note: cost_probes.py memory (memory.json): load+wait on a quiet line 63.9-0.9 ref; second independent load +2.6; stores to one address 35.8-0.9 ref each (repeat-address case only), +4.7 with wait 0. The 2026-10-10 load finding reported ~50 cycles for a dependent chase: unresolved discrepancy.
device_load_note: load-alu-grid.json: a load issued with no ALU instruction since the last wait completes ~45 units after issue (fast); after ALU work ~63 (slow); ALU instructions issued while it is pending defer completion to >= ALU issue + 31 (fast) / + 56 (slow) units. Fit on the 30-point grid.
memstate_note: memstate.json / tgmem.json: a memory instruction is slow when the group issued an ALU instruction while no load was outstanding since its previous memory instruction (stores release the pipe after issue). Slow device loads +~19 latency, threadgroup loads/stores +~19, device stores +~32 group-blocking issue. A device store right after a threadgroup store costs +16.5 (space switch; one measured combination).
quiet_note: Quiet-time rule (supersedes memstate_note): a memory instruction effectively starts no earlier than Q after the group's last ALU issue (Q ~20 units for loads and threadgroup ops, ~33.6 for device stores); loads then complete their fast latency after that start. A wait whose slot has nothing pending costs ~4.85 units (window probe, iadd + k x wait 1 + load); the jump at 32 such waits per repetition is the >512-byte loop-body step (wait_note).
wait_note: waits.json + waitruns.json: an idle wait costs ~4.89 units; waits in a run of >= 31 consecutive waits cost ~10.9 each. Not a body-size effect: 30 waits + iadd (564 B) and 16 waits, iadd, 16 waits (596 B) are fast, 8 waits + 6 iadd (532 B) is fast, 31 waits (516 B) and 31 waits + iadd (580 B) are slow. The run-length explanation also fails (16 waits, iadd, 16 waits concatenates into 32-wait runs and is fast); not modelled.
space_note: spaces.json: only transitions between a device store and a threadgroup access (either order) cost extra, ~6.7 units each; device<->threadgroup loads and threadgroup store -> device load cost nothing extra.
tg_defer_note: review2.json: tg load, iadd, wait = 42.0 and tg load, 8 iadd, wait = 53.6 units (tg load, wait = 22.9): ALU in flight defers threadgroup-load completion to >= ALU issue + ~20 units.
wait_drain_note: waitdrain.json, waitdrain-slots.json: a wait completes no earlier than ~17 units after the latest ALU result completes (iadd+wait 19.1, rcp+wait 21.9, simd_iadd+wait 37.2), and no earlier than ~4.9 after the previous wait issued (a second wait right after the first is free). Same for wait 0 and wait 1. Found from held-out memory kernels (heldout-mem24.json), whose error correlated with the number of waits.
